answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity bear a non-transferable cost. Concretely, every agent must post a bond that peers can slash, and vote weight is capped at the smallest bond among identities sharing one bond, so a farm must fund fresh collateral per identity and its sway stays flat. Identities that wander between keys leave bond-reuse traces peers reject. A new key alone is a bare cedar post: it anchors nothing without bonded history, and duplicate voices become a dune of empty names.
